content.value_statement: Security teams need a clear way to connect risks to practical controls. This skill structures threats, mitigations, gaps, and roadmaps for planning.
actual_capabilities: Maps threats to preventive, detective, and corrective controls.
Organizes controls by network, application, data, endpoint, process, and physical layers.
Identifies unmapped threats, weak coverage, and missing defense-in-depth.
Prioritizes remediation phases for critical and high impact threats.
Supports control effectiveness testing and reporting concepts.
limitations: Provides templates and guidance, not a complete runnable security platform.
Requires accurate threat data, control status, and cost estimates from the user.
Does not verify real control deployment without separate testing tools.
Does not replace formal risk assessment or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Remediation Work
use_cases.description: Map current threats to controls and rank gaps by impact, coverage, and implementation effort.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Coverage
use_cases.description: Check whether important threats have layered controls across application, data, endpoint, and process areas.

use_cases.title: Validate Control Effectiveness
use_cases.description: Define control tests, record results, and summarize effectiveness scores for management review.

prompt_templates.title: Map Basic Threats
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these threats and current controls. Map each threat to preventive, detective, and corrective mitigations.

prompt_templates.title: Find Coverage Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this mitigation plan. Identify unmapped threats, weak coverage, and missing defense-in-depth layers.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased remediation roadmap from these threats, controls, impact ratings, and cost estimates.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Risk Reduction
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these control options against budget limits. Recommend the mix that gives the highest risk reduction.

output_examples.input: A critical authentication threat has only password policy coverage.
output: Coverage gap: preventive control only, with no detective or corrective support.
Recommended controls: multi-factor authentication, login anomaly monitoring, and account recovery playbooks.
Priority: phase 1 because the threat is critical and current coverage is narrow.

output_examples.input: A data exfiltration threat has encryption but no monitoring.
output: Existing coverage protects stored data but does not detect misuse or outbound transfer.
Recommended controls: DLP monitoring, egress alerts, access reviews, and incident response steps.
Priority: high because detection and response are missing.

output_examples.input: A patch management control needs effectiveness reporting.
output: Suggested tests: patch age checks, vulnerable asset sampling, and exception review.
Report focus: pass rate, failed assets, overdue fixes, and ownership.
Follow-up: retest after remediation and update the control score.

best_practices: Start with a complete threat list and clear impact ratings.
Use layered controls across prevention, detection, and response.
Retest controls regularly and update coverage scores after changes.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on one control for a critical threat.
Do not assign controls without owners, status, and testing evidence.
Do not treat compliance mappings as proof of real effectiveness.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create threat-to-control mappings, gap lists, remediation priorities, and control effectiveness summaries.

faq.question: Can it replace a security assessment?
faq.answer: No. It structures the analysis, but experts must validate threats, control status, and business impact.

faq.question: Which frameworks can it support?
faq.answer: It can align planning with common control frameworks such as NIST CSF, CIS Controls, and MITRE D3FEND.

faq.question: Does it run security scans?
faq.answer: No. It provides mapping and planning templates, not active scanning or deployment verification.

faq.question: What inputs improve the output?
faq.answer: Threat descriptions, impact ratings, current controls, implementation status, costs, owners, and test results improve the analysis.

faq.question: Is it useful for budget planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare gaps, costs, and expected risk reduction to support investment decisions.
